newsitem.title: USA: MBA Refinancing Index peak reached, downturn eyed.
newsitem.headline: MBA Refinancing Index peak reached, downturn eyed.

text.p: The Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA) weekly refinancing index pierced 700, which would be this cycle's peak barring unexpected further mortgage rates declines, according to MBA Chief Economist David Lereah.
"As long as mortgage rates hold where they are, it's maxxed out," he said of the refinancing index.

The measure increased by 4.3 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis to 718.8 in the week ended August 8, compared with 689.3 the prior week. Lereah predicted a near-term decline in the index to the 500 level.

Mortgage rates had fallen 40 to 50 basis points in the past two months, generating a rush of home refinancings. But "The bullish economic data have exerted upward pressure on rates, keeping them up," Lereah noted. "The bullish inflation rates have stabilized (mortgage) rates. But I don't see (mortgage) rates coming down any time."
If rates do resume their downtrend, the refinancing index could hover around its current levels, the MBA economist said.
Refinancing activity represented 34.2 percent of total applications in the latest reporting week, up 0.2 percent from the prior week.
Total mortgage applications rose 3.7 percent from the prior week in the week ended August 8. The total was running 51.6 percent above the year-ago pace.

The average contract interest rate for 30-year fixed rate loans rose to 7.62 percent from 7.52 percent in the reporting week. For one-year adjustable-rate mortgages, the rate climbed to 5.80 percent from 5.71 percent, the MBA reported.
